failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or lower than the last 28-day mean, indicating the plateau/improvement did not continue.

mechanism_narrative: While Victoria remains in a steady-state lockdown regime, evidenced by persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL (~33-34%) and flat PARKS/TRANSIT series, retail mobility is structurally capped by stay-at-home orders, so RETAIL_REC will not materially improve over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean increases by more than 3 points relative to the prior 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 33%.

mechanism_narrative: April in Melbourne typically includes Easter and school holidays that would normally boost outdoor and retail activity; however, the flat PARKS series (~-80) suggests this seasonal uplift is being fully suppressed by lockdown measures, so no seasonal rebound in RETAIL_REC should occur this period.
failure_condition: PARKS or RETAIL_REC show a marked seasonal uplift (>10 points) in the week following the holiday period, contradicting the suppression hypothesis.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -52.6 to -46.3 between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 4 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC's following week mean does not increase correspondingly.

evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -73.6 to -70.7 between t-2w and t-1w
